messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: You should not take bupropion if you have seizures, an eating disorder, or suddenly stopped using alcohol, seizure medication, or sedatives. You should not take two medicines together that contain bupropion for example, if you take Wellbutrin for depression, you should not also take Contrave for weight control or Aplenzin for depression.
Do not use bupropion within 14 days before or 14 days after you have used a MAO inhibitors, such as isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue injection, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, or tranylcypromine.
Some young people (up to 24 years of age) have thoughts about suicide when first taking this medicine. Stay alert to changes in your mood or symptoms. Report any new or worsening symptoms to your doctor.
Triplet: ["Bupropion", "contraindicated with", "phenelzine"]

The relation 'contraindicated with' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug should not be used in combination with the substance or medication specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'contraindicated in': The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
B. 'should be avoided with': Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.
C. 'has maximum dose': The subject drug should not exceed the maximum dose specified by the object entity.
D. 'not approved for': The subject drug is not approved or not recommended for use in the patient population specified by the object entity.
E. 'has off label use': The subject drug is used for purposes not specifically approved or listed in the official medication guide, as specified by the object entity.
